risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management attributes the Agency Division's only marginal topline and bottom-line growth to 'the continued slowdown in the textile industry', with subdued business sentiment. The Agency division sells spinning machinery and the Textile division sells yarn, so a single industry downturn hits most of the Company's revenue base.
- 'Business sentiment remained subdued as customers adopted a cautious approach towards capital expenditure and new machinery investments, resulting in slower order conversions.' The Agency division's revenue depends on spinning mills committing to new machinery, so a capex pause converts directly into deferred orders; investment continued only 'selectively' and 'at a gradual pace'.
- Management flags 'a temporary impact of tariff rate revisions' on the Agency division and states that 'during the year, changes in tariff rates had a temporary impact on margins, though the situation subsequently stabilized' in the Textile division. Margins are therefore exposed to a policy variable outside the Company's control.
- 'The division continued to rely on high-quality imported cotton to ensure consistency in yarn quality ... as the quality of locally available cotton was not found to be fully suitable for the desired product standards.' Cost competitiveness was supported by 'the Government's extension of customs duty exemption on imported cotton up to December 2025' - an input-cost benefit with a stated end-date, and a structural dependence on imported raw material even when domestic cotton prices are stable.
- The Directors cite 'the prevailing global geopolitical uncertainties and war-related developments' as continuing to cast a cautious outlook on the industry, and note the 'impact of geopolitical uncertainties and tariff rate changes on global trade' against which direct exports grew. Yarn exports (including merchant exports) and Gears division exports are a material part of the book.
- The Company both earns foreign exchange (Rs. 4257.03 Lakhs) and incurs foreign exchange outgo, dominated by raw material imports (Rs. 2069.49 Lakhs of a Rs. 2259.47 Lakhs total). Currency and import-cost movements therefore feed into yarn conversion economics as well as export realisations.
- The Directors' Report technology-absorption disclosure returns blank entries for efforts towards technology absorption, benefits derived (product improvement, cost reduction, import substitution) and expenditure on research and development, leaving the businesses reliant on operating efficiency rather than proprietary product development for differentiation.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Textile (Yarn) division: drive profitability through internal measures aimed at enhancing productivity, process efficiency and operational discipline, plus focused cost optimization, rather than through topline growth.
- Continue sourcing high-quality imported cotton to keep yarn quality consistent, since locally available cotton was not found fully suitable for the desired product standards.
- Grow the direct export book on the strength of consistent product quality, timely deliveries and repeat orders from overseas customers.
- Reduce energy cost and dependence on grid power - 69.44% of energy …

hero.oneLiner: Super Sales India Limited is a diversified Coimbatore-region company operating three businesses - an Agency division marketing textile spinning machinery, a Textile (yarn) division and an Engineering (gears) division.
